title: React Tips and Tricks for Efficient Development
description: React tips for writing clean, efficient components: avoiding wrapper elements, using useCallback, and simplifying conditional rendering.

blocks.v: React Tips and Tricks for Efficient Development

None of what follows is a trick in the sense of being clever. They are the habits that separate a component someone else can pick up from one that has to be rewritten, and most of them cost nothing at the time and save a great deal later.
Insights: Why Efficient React Coding Matters
React is a powerful tool, but writing efficient code can make a big difference in your app’s performance and usability. Here’s why these best practices matter:

v: Better Performance: Optimised components render faster, improving user experience.
Easier Maintenance: Clean and consistent code is easier to update and debug.
Cost-Effective: Efficient code means shorter development times and fewer bugs.
Improved Accessibility: A streamlined DOM structure benefits all users.

blocks.v: Performance: Load Less, Render Less
The tips above keep code clean. These four keep a growing app fast.
Split Code with React.lazy and Suspense
Load a heavy component only when it is needed, instead of in the first bundle:
The same idea works per route: lazy-load each page so a visitor downloads only the page they open. Most routers and frameworks, Next.js included, split code by route for you.
Skip Re-renders with React.memo
React.memo re-renders a component only when its props change. It pairs with useCallback above: a memoised child is only skipped if the functions passed to it keep the same reference.
Cache Expensive Values with useMemo

useMemo recalculates a value only when its dependencies change. Use it for genuinely expensive work such as filtering or sorting a large list, not for simple arithmetic, where the memoisation costs more than it saves. In short: useMemo caches a value, useCallback caches a function, and React.memo caches a component's output.

blocks.v: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)
1. Why should I use React Fragments instead of wrapper <div> elements?React Fragments help reduce unnecessary DOM nodes, making your page load faster and your component structure cleaner.
2. How do default props improve my React app?Default props ensure your components function even if no values are passed, preventing undefined errors and improving user experience.
3. What is the impact of using useCallback on performance?useCallback prevents unnecessary re-renders by memoizing functions, which is particularly useful in apps with many child components.

4. Are inline styles bad for performance?Yes, because inline styles reduce page loading efficiency and caching capabilities. Using external styles or CSS-in-JS libraries like styled-components is better.
5. Should I always use export default for React components?While not mandatory, using export default for primary components simplifies imports and maintains consistency across your project.
6. Why is using unique keys in lists important for performance?Unique keys help React identify which items have changed, improving rendering efficiency and preventing layout issues.
